chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari and others, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
When you doubt in the Maghrib (prayer), so repeat it, and when you doubt in the Fajr (prayer), so repeat it.
ai.seo_question: What should one do if they doubt the number of rak'ahs during Maghrib or Fajr prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi outlines the principle of 'Ishkal' (doubt) specifically for the two-prayer (two-rak'ah) obligatory prayers, Maghrib and Fajr. In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling is distinct because these prayers have only two rak'ahs, making it impossible to have a 'doubt in the third' as seen in three-prayer or four-prayer prayers; thus, any doubt necessitates a full repetition to ensure the obligation is fulfilled. The transmission chain highlights the reliability of the Kufan school of hadith through scholars like Ibn Abi Umayr and Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari.
